description: Athlete feels like they're doing too many easy miles and wants more speed work added. Dean should add appropriate quality sessions while not overloading — and briefly explain the tradeoff.
inbound_sms: Honestly I feel like I'm doing a lot of easy miles. Can we add more speed work or tempo?

user.name: Leila
user.experience_level: intermediate — running 2 years, current 5k PR 23:30, wants sub-22

ground_truth.expected_change: Replace at least one easy run with a quality session. A 5k plan in week 3/9 with no quality work is unusual — adding intervals (400m or 800m reps at 7:13/mi) or a tempo run (3-4mi @ 8:02/mi) is appropriate. Keep one true easy day and the long run easy.
ground_truth.change_scope: Adjust this week and going forward. Quality 2x/week is reasonable for a 4-day athlete targeting a 5k.
must_include: a specific quality session added (e.g. intervals on Tuesday: 6x400m @ 7:13/mi)
the pace for the quality work (not just 'speed work')
keeping at least one easy day and the long run easy
must_not_include: making all four days quality sessions
adding quality on back-to-back days without a rest day between
a tempo run slower than easy pace
refusing to add quality because 'base phase' — Leila has 9 weeks and a specific goal
ground_truth.tradeoff_to_flag: Brief acknowledgment that easy miles build the aerobic base quality work draws from is fine — but one sentence max. Don't lecture. Just add the speed work.
ground_truth.notes: Leila's instinct is correct for 9 weeks out to a 5k — she should be doing intervals. All-easy weeks in week 3 with only 4 days/week is under-stimulating for a sub-22 goal. Dean should validate her instinct, add quality concretely (specific session with pace), and keep the response short. Do NOT over-explain the polarized training philosophy.
